title: An Inbox rename row reads the two names of that step (old → new), not the site's name now, after the site is renamed again
steps: S1: From the repo root at the commit under test, with TEST_DATABASE_URL set to a throwaway Postgres: node --test --test-reporter=tap packages/site/tracy-inbox/test/rows.test.mjs apps/tracy-web/test/site-event-notifications.test.mjs
S2: Read the lines for 'T14: each rename reads the two names of that step, not the name the site has now' and 'T14: a new address tells the team except the person who changed it'.
expect: Both tests report ok and the run ends with '# fail 0'.

The first: a row {oldSite: e2e04-wp.tracy.site, newSite: e2e04-wpx.tracy.site} on a site named e2e04-wp.tracy.site today reads 'Renamed e2e04-wp.tracy.site to e2e04-wpx.tracy.site' (pre-fix: '… to e2e04-wp.tracy.site'); a row with no newSite still reads the name now.
The second: PUT /api/sites/:key/address writes team.site_renamed rows whose data holds both oldSite and newSite.
evidence: E2E dev 04/10 E9.1b (tasks/evidence/e2e-dev-0410/bugs.md item 7, E9/b-list-0.json): renaming wp → wpx → wp left a first row 'Renamed e2e04-wp.tracy.site to e2e04-wp.tracy.site', because the row stored only oldSite and the Inbox drew the 'to' side from the site's name at read time.
fence: sites/route.js onRenamed stores data.newSite beside data.oldSite; tracy-inbox rows.ts describe() draws team.site_renamed from data.newSite (fallback: siteName for rows written before); mail/letters/team.js does the same.

tests: T14: each rename reads the two names of that step, not the name the site has now
T14: a new address tells the team except the person who changed it
